fatal_errors: The proposed Ti addition does not reconstruct the target intervention of SPS at 1000 °C applied to ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder.
No Ti concentration or fixed base composition is specified, so the intervention is not reproducible as written.
The experiment omits density measurement despite requiring retention of low density.
High-temperature oxidation temperature, exposure time, atmosphere, and kinetic acceptance criteria are unspecified.
The cited evidence does not isolate Ti addition as the cause of simultaneous mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation improvements.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested multi-property lightweight-alloy objective and proposes a broadly plausible compositional comparison, but it has little agreement with the hidden target. It misses the SPS-temperature intervention, MgAlTiVFeCo BCC starting state, oxide barrier phases, densification/passivation mechanism, 800–1000 °C process window, 900 °C oxidation test, and the quantitative density, hardness, oxidation-kinetic, and electrochemical outcomes. Its mechanism relies mainly on generic high-entropy solid-solution claims and does not explain why Ti should improve all three properties. E1 concerns Cu variation in an alloy already containing Ti, E2 only indirectly supports Ti substitution for lower density, and E3 reports favorable Ti-containing alloys without a Ti-free control; none establishes the proposed causal intervention. The control concept is useful, but fixed composition, Ti dose, processing conditions, density measurement, oxidation kinetics, and quantitative falsification thresholds are needed for a discriminating test.
